chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-ʿAbbās together, from Saʿdān ibn Muslim, who said:

I was in the bathhouse, in the middle room, when Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام entered upon me. He had depilatory substance on him, and he was wearing a waist-wrapper over the depilatory substance. He said, "Peace be upon you." So I returned the greeting of peace to him, and hurriedly went into the room in which there was the basin, then I washed myself and came out.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam عليه السلام mentioned in the report
key_terms.إِزَارٌ: a waist-wrapper or lower garment used for covering
key_terms.النُّورَةُ: depilatory substance used for removing hair
key_terms.الْحَمَّامِ: the bathhouse or place of washing
key_terms.الْحَوْضُ: a basin or pool of water used for washing

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām describe about bathhouse etiquette and covering?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident in the bathhouse involving Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, describing his state and conduct upon entering and greeting with salām. It reflects etiquette, covering in the bathhouse, and practical aspects connected to cleanliness and bathing.
